title: Dynamic KV-slab allocator + length-aware batch packing for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Our continuous-batching scheduler experiences tail latency and GPU OOMs on mixed-length request streams where short prompts interleave with long-response generations. Current behavior packs by arrival time and drops KV cache aggressively, causing re-computation for long sequences and head-of-line blocking for short requests.

Goal: Implement a length-aware packing policy + a dynamic slab allocator for KV cache that preserves long-sequence context while offloading cold KV slabs to host/persistent memory. The solution should reduce tail latency for short requests, reduce total GPU memory footprint, and keep throughput within +/-5% of baseline for steady-state workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) 95th percentile latency for short (<=64-token) requests decreases by at least 25% under mixed traffic (30% short, 70% long) compared to current scheduler.
2) GPU memory pressure events (OOMs or emergency evictions) drop to zero during 24-hour stress tests configured with realistic open-source models.
3) End-to-end throughput stays within 95-105% of current throughput on baseline batchable workloads.
4) No correctness regressions: outputs identical (bitwise token generation sequences) for deterministic model variants in controlled tests.
5) Feature guarded and rollout-able via runtime-1.27 feature flag with canary and automatic rollback metrics.
design_notes:
High-level components:
- Length-aware packing: classify incoming requests into buckets (short<=64, medium<=512, long>512). Maintain per-bucket micro-queues and a packing loop that prioritizes short queues to avoid head-of-line blocking while still enabling cross-bucket packing when it improves utilization.
- Dynamic KV-slab allocator: allocate KV cache as slabs partitioned by sequence-length group and user/session hotness. Slabs can be compressed (int8 or FP16 depending on model support) and asynchronously offloaded to pinned host memory when cold.
- Async KV transfers: use CUDA streams + pinned host pages to migrate cold slabs with backpressure; warms on predicted reuse via simple LRU-with-prefetch heuristic driven by sequence-len histograms.
- Eviction policy: avoid evicting the most recently extended long sequences; prefer evicting cold slabs for sessions with no activity for >t_idle.
- Adaptive per-slot max_tokens: dynamically limit max_tokens_per_request for heavily contended slots to maintain latency SLOs (configurable per-customer).

Notes on trade-offs: offloading reduces GPU memory but adds host transfer latency on warmups — we mitigate with prefetch heuristics and by prioritizing short requests which rarely need large warmed caches. Compression reduces memory but must be cheap to decompress on critical path; explore kernel-level int8 paths where supported.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): implement per-bucket micro-queues and a synthetic load generator to emulate mixed-length traffic. Gather histograms and define thresholds.
Phase 2 (prototype, 2 weeks): add length-aware packer in the scheduler and measure latency/throughput impact. No KV changes yet.
Phase 3 (kv-slab allocator, 2 weeks): implement slab allocation APIs, compression paths (FP16 fallback), and async host offload with warmup prefetch hooks.
Phase 4 (integration + rollout, 2 weeks): wire allocator into scheduler, add feature flag, canary rollout to 5% of traffic, monitor metrics and iterate.
Phase 5 (runbook + docs, 1 week): update runbooks, observability dashboards, and SDK knobs for customers.

Key milestones: micro-queue telemetry, KV offload correctness tests, canary pass criteria.
metrics_and_dashboards:
Add these metrics to the runtime dashboard:
- batch_size_distribution_by_bucket (histogram)
- kv_slab_count_by_bucket (gauge)
- kv_offload_rate_success/fail (counter)
- host_warmup_latency_p95 (ms)
- short_request_tail_latency_p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- gpu_memory_headroom (MiB)
- emergency_eviction_count (counter)
- feature_flag_rollout_percentage (gauge)

Also create an alert: if short_request_p95 > target AND emergency_eviction_count > 0 for 10 minutes, auto-roll back canary.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for allocator correctness and compression round-trips.
Integration tests with small-scale multi-GPU cluster to validate async offload correctness under churn.
End-to-end perf jobs: run 6-hour synthetic mixes (30/70 short/long, 50/50, and extreme 80/20 long) against models used in runtime-1.27 matrix.
A/B canary with traffic shadowing on 5% of production; once stable, progress to 25% then 100%.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Host offload warmup causes latency spikes for long sessions. Mitigation: conservative prefetch heuristics + enable knob to pin popular session slabs during canary.
Risk: Compression/decompression adds CPU overhead. Mitigation: only enable for models/hardware where hardware-accelerated paths exist; measure CPU impact and gate behind config.
Risk: Complexity in scheduler causing regressions. Mitigation: keep initial packer simple, heavy telemetry, revertible feature flag.
